states.name: Open_IdleAvailable
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds at least one idle connection but fewer than MaxIdle; connReqs is empty

states.name: Open_IdleFull
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds exactly MaxIdle idle connections (the channel is full); connReqs is empty

states.name: Open_NoIdle_BelowCap
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds no idle connection; connReqs is empty; openingConns < maxActive

states.name: Open_NoIdle_AtCap
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds no idle connection; connReqs is empty; openingConns >= maxActive

states.name: Open_Waiting_AtCap
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds no idle connection; connReqs is non-empty; openingConns >= maxActive

states.name: Open_Waiting_BelowCap
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds no idle connection; connReqs is non-empty; openingConns < maxActive

states.name: Open_Waiting_IdleAvailable
states.condition: conns is non-nil and holds at least one idle connection; connReqs is non-empty

states.name: Closed
states.condition: conns is nil (Release has completed): factory, ping and close are nil

events.gist: a caller calls Get() on the pool
a caller calls Put(conn) with a non-nil connection that it earlier obtained from Get
a caller calls Close(conn) with a non-nil connection that it earlier obtained from Get
a caller calls Ping(conn) with a non-nil connection
a caller calls Release() on the pool
a caller calls Len() on the pool

notes: Each cell describes one call run to completion in the given state. Unless a cell says otherwise, Ping is configured (non-nil), IdleTimeout > 0, MaxIdle >= 1 and the idle connections are not expired. Where the outcome depends on a guard (for example whether the last idle connection is taken, or a callback returns an error), write the main branch as the disposition and the other branches in the note. A transition target is the state after the call returns. Connections are values of type interface{} handed in by the caller.
